questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake—at least three-fourths of your total stopping power.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops come from using both brakes smoothly and gradually without locking up either tire.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems are more serious on a motorcycle than on a car. Always do a complete check of your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Drag your feet on the ground.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet or point them downward, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen in any condition. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothes both day and night.

questions.question: Which should you check before riding?

options.text: How much cushion your seat has.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Orange, red, yellow, and green make you easier to see. Wear bright colors no matter what time of day you ride.

questions.question: Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Give yourself time and space to spot and react to dangers.
Help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself time and space to spot and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or move if the car ahead stops suddenly. Extra space also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as without a passenger.
Tell the passenger the rules after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be equipped and adjusted for a passenger. It needs separate footrests for the passenger and a large enough seat. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Turns the same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be ridden on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It is fine as long as you ride slowly.
Alcohol may still be in your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol may still be in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour on average. The time needed varies from person to person. It is safest to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. Even one drink per hour can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: One benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will stay in good condition if you maintain it properly and do regular checks.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and you control it with your right hand.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Weave across the lane to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where to position the motorcycle in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is so much traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many crashes happen when motorcyclists and other drivers meet there.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, stay at least this far behind the vehicle ahead:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, maintain a two-second following distance. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Bright clothes help you stay visible day and night.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, wear a jacket:

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your eyes and face the best. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not legally need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is recommended.

questions.question: What can you do in a no passing zone on a motorcycle?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if the pass finishes before another vehicle comes.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in a no passing zone. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like all other vehicles.
It helps other drivers see you.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always look over your shoulder to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator be more visible?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright colors with reflective material. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What happens when you take corners too fast?

options.text: You may go into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You usually stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you start a turn or curve.
